system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student in computational genomics and functional genomics who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given the following experiment that investigates whether late-layer embeddings from Evo2 — a DNA foundation model trained autoregressively on 8.8 trillion nucleotide tokens across all domains of life — encode functionally meaningful information about human genes. The baseline experiment fetches the promoter (2kb upstream of TSS) and coding sequence (CDS) for human genes in two functional classes: DNA repair genes (from KEGG pathways hsa03430/hsa03420/hsa03440/hsa03410) and tumor suppressor genes (curated from the Cancer Gene Census). It extracts mean-pooled late-layer (blocks.28.mlp.l3) embeddings from a frozen Evo2-7B model and trains a small MLP classifier to distinguish these two classes (baseline AUROC ~0.78). The core research question is: do Evo2 embeddings encode a biologically meaningful functional landscape? The most interesting experiments focus on SUPERVISED CLUSTERING and CLASSIFICATION: training probes (linear, MLP, SVM), cross-validation strategies, feature importance, decision boundary analysis, learning curves, and understanding what drives supervised separability between functional classes. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS: (1) Do NOT add new gene classes or fetch additional genes — the dataset is already cached. (2) All experiments must reuse the cached dataset.json and embeddings_evo2_7b.npy files from run_0/data/. (3) Do NOT modify sequence inputs or embedding extraction — only modify analysis, clustering, and visualization code. (4) Do NOT propose promoter vs CDS comparisons — focus on what the existing embeddings reveal about functional organization.
